successCriteria.description: No local `RepositoryError` or `UniqueConstraintError` class definitions remain anywhere under `src/modules/policy/`; both symbols are obtained by importing from the employee module's public entry point (`src/modules/employee/index.ts`).

Every policy-module reference to `RepositoryError`/`UniqueConstraintError` (in `policy.errors.ts` and `policy.repository.ts`) resolves to the single employee-module definition, so `PolicyNotFoundError instanceof RepositoryError` and the `DUPLICATE_POLICY` `UniqueConstraintError` remain true with no duplicate class identity.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Policy module section no longer states that `policy.errors.ts` contains `RepositoryError`/`UniqueConstraintError`; it accurately reflects that these are imported from the employee module and that `policy.errors.ts` defines only `PolicyNotFoundError`.

constraints: The employee module's public entry point (`src/modules/employee/index.ts`) is the single source of truth for `RepositoryError` and `UniqueConstraintError`; the policy module must import these symbols from that entry point and must not re-define them.
Cross-module imports must go through the declared public entry point (`index.ts`) only — no deep imports of `employee.errors.ts` from the policy module.
The refactor must not change the observable error semantics: `PolicyNotFoundError` keeps code `POLICY_NOT_FOUND`, and the `DUPLICATE_POLICY` `UniqueConstraintError` keeps its code and message.
No circular dependency may be introduced between the policy and employee modules (employee must not import from policy).

entityInvariants.invariant: Defined exactly once, in the employee module, and re-exported from its public entry point; it is the single base class for all repository error types, so `PolicyNotFoundError` and `UniqueConstraintError` share one class identity.
Defined exactly once, in the employee module, and re-exported from its public entry point; policy code instantiates it with code `DUPLICATE_POLICY` and it remains `instanceof RepositoryError`.
Remains the only error class defined in `policy.errors.ts`, extends the imported `RepositoryError`, and carries code `POLICY_NOT_FOUND`.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: `RepositoryError` and `UniqueConstraintError` must be the exact symbols exported from the employee module's public entry point — no local re-declaration, re-export, or aliasing that would create a second class identity.

The policy module's error layout must match the employee module's established pattern: a base `RepositoryError` plus typed subclasses, with the base and shared `UniqueConstraintError` owned by the employee module and consumed via its entry point.

The Policy module documentation must accurately describe the current error ownership (imported `RepositoryError`/`UniqueConstraintError`, locally-defined `PolicyNotFoundError`), consistent with the actual source files.

integrationPoints.why: The public entry point that re-exports `RepositoryError` and `UniqueConstraintError`; the policy module's error and repository files import these symbols from here.
Defines `PolicyNotFoundError` and imports `RepositoryError` from the employee entry point; must contain no local `RepositoryError`/`UniqueConstraintError` definitions.
Consumes `UniqueConstraintError` from the employee entry point when mapping pg `23505` violations to `DUPLICATE_POLICY`.
